name: CA Continuous
miniText: What changes when a cellular rule acts on real-valued states instead of bits? NetLogo CA Continuous averages a cell and its nearest neighbors, adds a chosen constant, and keeps the fractional part to obtain the next state. Values are plotted in successive rows as a space-time diagram. Kaneko [1] supplies the coupled-map-lattice context explicitly cited in the original Info, Wolfram [2] provides a discrete cellular comparison, and Peitgen and colleagues [3] explain iterated-map and numerical-chaos concepts. The precision control quantizes the nominally continuous values, while finite arithmetic and a bounded lattice impose further constraints. The update is deterministic; varied patterns are not evidence of random forcing. The experiment illustrates the interaction of local coupling, nonlinear iteration, and numerical precision, rather than a validated physical diffusion law or literally infinite state space.
